A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 31 pages, including Appendices A–G. Text extraction and visual comparison support a reliable comparison of their equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic and semi-synthetic experiments, calibration diagnostics, and a COVID-19 observational data analysis in Section 6 and Appendices F–G.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental and data-analysis results, including benchmark comparisons and the COVID-19 case study.

M1.justification: Appendix D.1, Eq. (61), revises the specified copula update weight from alpha_N=(2-1/N)/(N+1) to (2-1/(n+N))/(n+N+1). This changes the stated resampling procedure's dependence on observed sample size, while retaining the broader MP-OSPC construction.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic design, IHDP, 77 ACIC 2016 datasets, and COVID-19 lockdown case study. Dataset, task, and scenario coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same CausalPFN naive plug-ins, TabPFN-based MP plug-ins, PFN/MP combinations, and A-IPTW references. No comparator is added or removed within an experiment.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 substantively revises the stated copula resampling learning-rate schedule to incorporate n. This is a reported setting revision; splits, metrics, default N=B=100, and other experimental settings remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The MP convergence diagnostics, nuisance-posterior concentration checks, hyperparameter and copula sensitivity analyses, resource measurements, and real-world case study are retained without new or removed analyses.

E5.justification: Repeated-run counts and uncertainty reporting are unchanged, including 10-run diagnostics, 40-run synthetic comparisons, and the 100-split IHDP evaluation with standard errors.

E6.justification: The empirical scores, plotted curves, and reported findings in Section 6 and Appendices F–G are unchanged. Tables 2–5 and the experimental figures contain no added, removed, or corrected result entries.

T1.justification: Section 5.4 replaces the stated O_P((n+N)^(-1/2)) concentration rate with O_P(n^(-1/2)) + O_P((n+N)^(-1/2)) = O_P(n^(-1/2)), explicitly connecting it to the revised learning-rate schedule. This changes the mathematical reasoning locally; the substantive theorem statements and appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning prior-induced confounding bias, MP-OSPC calibration, frequentist consistency, and finite-sample uncertainty.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 refines the explanation of MP concentration by distinguishing sample-size and finite-step contributions and linking them to the learning rate. It replaces v2's emphasis on approximation error controllable through N, while retaining the attribution of BvM failures primarily to the underlying PFNs.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 updates the implementation formula and accompanying decay-rate discussion to include observed sample size n. Other implementation details, propensity truncation, hardware information, and code/data access links are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and novelty positioning are unchanged. The revised concentration discussion uses works already cited in v2.

P1.justification: Several posterior-related uses of 'convergence' become 'concentration', and one paragraph in Section 5.4 is locally rewritten. Section ordering and narrative structure remain unchanged; the version/date stamp is updated.

P2.justification: Local paragraph spacing, line wrapping, and equation width change around the revised passages on pages 8 and 20. Figures 1–15 and Tables 1–5 retain their displays, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: Including sample-size dependence in Eq. (61) and aligning Section 5.4's concentration discussion with that schedule improves the coherence and reproducibility of the technical specification. The revised explanation better distinguishes sample-size effects from finite-step approximation. These are limited improvements: the central claims, proofs, empirical evidence, and applicability limitations remain unchanged.
